original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost, so decoder copy cost is the lever this card targets. This package prices the Eisenstein (F4/Eisenstein-phase) decoder route under the inherited accounting: the certified necessary-condition screen says any beating supplier needs total copy cost C <= 31 at some stage count (sup bracket 31.0635 at s=7, window h=7; h=10 gives C <= 29 at s <= 35), while every clean support alphabet costs exactly 40 (two independent sharp witnesses). The route therefore survives only if a non-clean decoder with C <= 31 exists; the prize is capped by the selected assembly's bit side at kappa <= 1733427039589844234749/1001733427039589844234749 = 0.001730427469823602 (+3.45% over the selected 0.001672660197076918).
stop_rule: Stop when (a) the certified threshold screen covers every legal window h in [7,40] and every odd stage count s (scan plus exact rational tail closure), (b) the clean-class floor 40 is proven with sharp witnesses, and (c) negative controls pass; or immediately if a candidate supplier beats the screen, or if the screen's assumptions are contradicted by an existing result.
evidence: research/eisenstein-phase-cost-screen/verify.py passes in ~21s (Python 3.12, stdlib only, no randomness): Part A replays the 240-root geometry (40 lines, flat census 1/40/240/90/360/40/1, all line-spanned flats nonsingular, a 7-clique exists so any legal pattern has rank >= 7). Part B proves the clean-class floor: on all 7033 clean ordered flat pairs the per-rectangle charge equals |R cap A| (tight everywhere), and two independent pattern-legal witnesses cost exactly 40 (ten orthogonal 4-line frames; 40 clean stars). Part C certifies, for every window h in [7,40] and every odd s, closed-form rational brackets on the exact copy-cost threshold C*(s,h) (the beat condition is linear in C), with direct certified confirmation and an exact rational tail closure (binomial-series increment bound, exact partial sums to P=200, exact quadratic minimum beyond) covering all s beyond the closure point; sup over the screen is 31.063467310837773 at s=7 h=7, so any beating supplier needs C <= 31 at s <= 61 (h=7 row; h=10: C <= 29 at s <= 35). Part D shows every screen argmax point clears the selected bit side 0.001733427039589844, so the prize is capped at kappa <= 0.001730427469823602 (+3.45%). Part E: four negative controls (closed-form/direct cross-validation, doubled-b flip, tampered-pattern census change, naive-partition illegality and star self-loop sensitivity). Not done: no supplier was built; the non-clean window C in [22,31] is open; no kappa changed.

open_questions.question: Does a pattern-legal 40x40 F2-valued decoder exist with total copy cost C <= 31 whose support is NOT clean (i.e. some clean-class hypothesis fails), and does its full frame/restoration bill stay within the screen?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The screen is a necessary condition: the entire remaining upside of the Eisenstein phase route lives in the non-clean window C in [22,31] at s <= 61. Settling it either yields the first Eisenstein-supplied assembly (kappa up to the bit cap 0.001730427469823602) or closes the route under the current accounting.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the clean-class dichotomy: enumerate minimal non-clean supports (a nonorthogonal pair read by a common rectangle) and certify their minimum copy cost with the same pairing-rank machinery; if the minimum exceeds 31 the route is closed.

open_questions.question: Can the quadratic-phase normal form (PR #831) actually realize a candidate decoder's phase labels on nondegenerate alternating blocks at the frame level required by the assembly template?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR #831 removed the interface obstruction at the trace-form level, but no one has checked that a concrete cheap decoder's labels compile through the alternating-compatible normal form without extra frames or adapters that would break the C <= 31 budget.
open_questions.first_step: Take the cheapest abstract decoder surviving the screen (if any) and run the f4-alternating-interface compilation on its labels, charging every added frame.
